column3: MT 102:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. Close to the Hebrew; “if he grows faint” is rendered “when he is faint.”
Close to the Hebrew; “hurry, answer me” is rendered “answer me quickly.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they have come to an end” is rendered “have been consumed,” and “burned” as “scorched.”
Close to the Hebrew; “vegetation” is rendered “grass,” and “I have forgotten from eating my food” as “I forget to eat my bread.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the sound of my groaning” is rendered “the loudness of my groaning.”
“Desert owl” (an unclean bird whose identity is uncertain) is rendered “pelican.”
Close to the Hebrew; “isolated” is rendered “lonely,” and “roof” as “housetop.”
“By me they have sworn” is rendered “have used my name as a curse.”
Close to the Hebrew; “food” is rendered “bread.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“You sit [enthroned]” is rendered “abide,” and “the remembrance of you” as “Your name.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “they show favor to her dust” is rendered “feel pity for her dust.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “he has turned to” is rendered “He has regarded.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a generation later” is rendered “the generation to come,” and NASB makes the second line a purpose clause (“That a people … may praise”).
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “the sons of death” is rendered “those who were doomed to death.”
NASB adds “That men may” to the infinitive “to recount.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; “he has humbled” is rendered “He has weakened.”
NASB marks verses 24–28 as quoted speech; “lift me up” is rendered “take me away,” and “in a generation of generations” as “throughout all generations.”
Close to the Hebrew; “before” is rendered “Of old.”
Close to the Hebrew; “and they may pass away” is rendered “and they will be changed.”
Close to the Hebrew; “you [are] he” is rendered “You are the same.”
Close to the Hebrew; “they will dwell” is rendered “will continue.”
